analysis.title: Guide to the Markets - EMEA (data as of 30 September 2026)
key_insights: The 97-page chart book covers the global economy, equities, fixed income, other assets, ESG and investing principles. It is built from charts and carries almost no prose commentary. Most conclusions below come from labelled chart values in the text.
S&P 500 12-month forward P/E was 19,1x on 30 Sep 2026 against a long-run average of 16,7x. Shiller CAPE was 40,6x against a 27,3x average since 1990, and price-to-book was 5,4x against 3,2x.

MSCI Europe forward P/E was 14,1x against a 14,3x average. CAPE was 20,2x against 19,3x and price-to-book 2,5x against 2,1x. Europe valuations are close to their own history, while the US is well above its own.
MSCI China forward P/E was 10,2x against an 11,5x average.

Latest headline inflation in the heatmap, read as August 2026 year on year: eurozone 3,2%, US 3,4%, UK 3,1%, Japan 1,9%, China 0,8%, India 4,8%, Brazil 4,2%. Eurozone inflation is up from 1,7-1,9% in early 2026, and the US and eurozone figures are well above their autumn 2025 readings.

Brent futures on the Guide's oil page are 104 for 1 month, 90 for 6 months and 83 for 12 months, a steeply backwardated curve. The US, Russia and Saudi Arabia each produce 11,7% to 15,9% of global crude.

Several pages are devoted to AI. They cover hyperscaler capex estimates, hyperscaler cash flow and net debt issuance, AI-related index weights in the US, EM, Europe and Japan, S&P 500 vs hyperscaler vs semiconductor EPS growth, and AI token and GPU rental costs. Debt issuance by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle includes $30bn issued by Meta and Blue Owl Capital.

Market concentration pages show the tech sector and US weight in global equities. They list the top 10 US benchmark names (Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Broadcom, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Tesla and others) against the top EM names (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Tencent, Alibaba and others).

Fiscal pages cover US federal deficit, net interest and net debt with CBO forecasts, German Defence Fund and infrastructure fund spending, EU defence spending, the UK's fiscal position after the October 2024 employer National Insurance hike, and government debt for the US, eurozone, Germany and the UK.

The US effective tariff rate chart compares the 'Liberation Day' rate, current policy and a pre-Supreme Court ruling rate, so tariff policy has changed since the earlier regime. The text does not give the rate levels.

Fixed income pages cover yields, spreads, high yield default rates, term premium, yield cushion, EM debt and returns. They show the 10-year Treasury yield split into real yield and inflation expectations, and the same split for Bunds.
US household equity ownership is concentrated. Equity share of net worth is 12% for the bottom 50% and for the 50-90% group, 31% for the 90-99% group and 49% for the top 1%.

Long-run real annualised returns for 1900-2025 are equities 6,9%, bonds 1,7% and cash 0,5%. For 2000-2025 they are 5,5%, 2,0% and -0,6%. MSCI World has had average intra-year drops of 14,6% (median 10,5%) yet positive calendar-year returns in 29 of 40 years.

J.P. Morgan's 2026 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (10-15 year, nominal EUR) are charted for euro cash, euro government bonds, euro investment-grade credit, 60/40 and 50/30/20 portfolios, infrastructure, US and eurozone large cap, European core real estate, China, EM and Japan. The text gives no values.
Regional revenue exposure: S&P 500 is 59% US, 20% Asia/Pacific and 14% Europe. MSCI Europe is 49% Europe and 21% US. FTSE All-Share is 26% UK and 22% US. TOPIX is 50% Japan and 20% Asia/Pacific.

The US dollar page ties the dollar to interest rate differentials and says the current dollar cycle began after the dollar peaked in January 2025. It compares equity and currency contributions to relative US equity performance across past cycles.

Chinese household assets are 63% property and 25% cash and deposits, with 4% in equities and mutual funds. The Guide pairs this with weak consumer-goods PPI, new home prices and export data by destination.

ESG pages cover climate risk, grid spending, copper supply and demand, data centre electricity consumption, carbon prices against the IMF's USD 85 recommendation for 2030, the energy mix, EV sales and mineral content, and green, social and sustainable bond issuance.
earnings_insights: The Guide charts 2026 consensus EPS growth for the US, Europe, UK, Japan and EM, and US hyperscaler and semiconductor EPS growth for 2024, 2025 and 2026F. No numeric earnings figures are given in the text. The footnote says 2026 earnings forecasts are adjusted to remove the impact of the revaluation of equity stakes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Latest cell in the eurozone row of the headline inflation heatmap. It is up from 1,7% in early 2026 and above the 2% target.
Latest cell in the US row of the heatmap. It peaked at 4,2% earlier in 2026.
Latest cell in the UK row of the heatmap.
Latest cell in the Japan row of the heatmap.
Latest cell in the China row of the heatmap, close to zero inflation.

macro_indicators.indicator: Brent crude futures (1 month / 6 month / 12 month)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The futures curve is backwardated: front-month prices sit well above later contracts.

risk_factors: US equity valuations are high against history: S&P 500 forward P/E 19,1x vs 16,7x average, CAPE 40,6x vs 27,3x.
Index concentration. The Guide charts the tech sector's weight and the US weight in global equities, and the top 10 US and EM index constituents.
Rising government debt, net interest costs and bond supply, with ageing populations adding fiscal pressure in the US, UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain and Japan.
Inflation re-acceleration in the eurozone, US and UK in 2026, and a higher oil price curve at the front end.
AI-related cost pressure and heavy hyperscaler debt issuance, shown in the AI demand and hyperscaler issuance pages.
Tariffs and trade policy, shown in the US effective tariff rate and import price charts.
charts_described: S&P 500 forward P/E: 19,1x on 30 Sep 2026 against a 16,7x average.
MSCI Europe forward P/E: 14,1x on 30 Sep 2026 against a 14,3x average.
MSCI China forward P/E: 10,2x on 30 Sep 2026 against an 11,5x average.
Brent futures: 104 for 1 month, 90 for 6 months and 83 for 12 months.
Long-term asset returns: real annualised returns of equities 6,9%, bonds 1,7% and cash 0,5% for 1900-2025.
MSCI World annual returns and intra-year declines: average intra-year drop of 14,6%, positive annual returns in 29 of 40 years.
vol_and_positioning: The Guide charts the VIX against macro hedge fund performance relative to MSCI Europe, and hedge fund style returns in the 2000, 2008 and 2020 bear markets. No level is given in the text.
US long-term equity mutual fund and ETF three-month net flows are charted against the S&P 500 under the heading 'Avoid selling at the bottom'.
geopolitical: The oil page shows crude production shares for the US, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran, the UAE and OPEC ex-Saudi Arabia, Iran and UAE, with Iran at 4,7%.
The US trade page charts the effective tariff rate under 'Liberation Day', current policy and a pre-Supreme Court ruling scenario.
The gold page labels three drivers of gold's rise: geopolitics and fiscal concerns, falling real rates and stagflation.

The shock-returns page lists 60/40 returns after Gulf war I, the Asian bank crisis, the Russian default, 9-11, Gulf war II, Lehman, the eurozone crisis, the US debt downgrade, Brexit, Covid-19 and Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
